#84082. Multiparameter quantum bounds for entanglement-assisted aperture synthesis

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (274 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Multiparameter quantum bounds for entanglement-assisted aperture synthesis

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (274 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

In a recent development, arXiv:2609.10111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement-assisted optical interferometry promises diffraction-limited imaging over baselines where light cannot be physically combined, but its estimation-theoretic bounds exist only for a single visibility on one baseline. This work formulates the multiparameter quantum estimation problem for an M-station array. A reduction lemma indicates that the multimode quantum Fisher information (QFI) equals the mean photon number times the QFI of a single delocalized photon, making the problem finite-dimensional. The local photon-number superselection rule erases all phase information from the bare state; shared entanglement restores a fraction f(r)=r/(1+r) of the QFI on a baseline supplied with r pairs, a benchmark that applies to every pair of the array. The QFI matrix and its mean Uhlmann curvature show numerically that a point source is measurement-compatible, whereas every extended-source model examined is incompatible; a semidefinite-programming evaluation shows that the Holevo bound exceeds the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative bound by up to ~24% for three stations and by 4-8% for larger arrays and for CHARA. An explicit collective receiver, a numerically optimised global linear-optical network with photon counting, attains a weighted variance within 2-9% of the Holevo bound, over an order of magnitude below an explicit pairwise receiver, and a noisy-resource threshold gives the break-even baseline (~22 km for illustrative parameters) beyond which distributed entanglement beats direct transmission. Finally, allocating a finite entanglement budget has a closed-form proportional (square-root-law) solution for a per-baseline fringe cost, whereas for the source-parameter variance under an explicit photon budget the routing of photons matters far more than the entanglement split. These results recast quantum aperture synthesis as collective multiparameter estimation, illustrated on CHARA.

#84079. Adapting Generalist Vehicle Models for High-Speed MPC Across Terrains

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (257 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Adapting Generalist Vehicle Models for High-Speed MPC Across Terrains

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (257 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2607.13319v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-speed off-road autonomy requires precise closed-loop control for a target vehicle while remaining robust across changing terrains. Recent forward kinodynamic (FKD) prediction foundation models suggest a promising path, starting from a generalist model and specializing it to the target platform. However, effective specialization remains challenging, as it often requires substantial real-world data, and models adapted to one setting can still overfit to specific terrains or driving regimes. We present OptCar (Optimized Car), a recipe for bridging the gap from generalist to specialist FKD models that preserves cross-terrain generalization while optimizing performance for a specific vehicle. OptCar introduces a transformer FKD architecture that uses FiLM to condition multi-step predictions on a single dynamics context token summarizing recent state-action history. It then specializes the generalist model using limited real-world data and targeted synthetic rollouts from environment-specific system identification. In closed-loop model predictive control (MPC) experiments across three terrains and an out-of-distribution cart-pulling task, the largest gains appear at 6 m/s, the highest speed evaluated and the regime in which slip dominates tracking error. On vegetation + dirt, the most slip-diverse terrain, OptCar reduces 6 m/s trajectory tracking error by roughly 55% relative to AnyCar fine-tuned on real data alone, and remains the most accurate even when an unseen cart payload changes the dynamics. With 5 minutes of real data per terrain, OptCar is competitive on road with a specialist trained on 30 minutes of road data and outperforms it when the terrain changes. Project Page : https://amrl.cs.utexas.edu/optcar/.

Sources indicate that arXiv:2609.05472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide an exact analytical benchmarks into measuring the quantum information spreading by introducing N-operator correlators. Leveraging the idea from N-point correlation function from cosmology, we formulate a generalized Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC), called N-Operator Correlator (NOC). Such formulation can reduce the effect of restricted analysis associated with selecting only two operators for OTOC. NOC can take into account a larger set of measurement probes in measuring the degree of quantum information spreading. We demonstrate these concepts with two analytically tractable systems with computing thermal averages of operator time evolutions at a finite temperature: a single qubit in longitudinal field and isotropic XXX model with a transverse field, two-qubit system. Our analytical benchmark serves as a basic introduction to generalized operator correlators in quantum mechanics.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (232 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Real-time fall detection based on vision for low-power edge platforms

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (232 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2607.12909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Falling detection is vital for elderly care and intelligent surveillance; however, prevailing vision-based approaches predominantly frame it as static pose classification or discrete temporal pattern matching, fundamentally overlooking the instability dynamics of the human support system. This paper proposes a physics-informed falling detection framework that recasts falling as a stability-loss event in a coupled dynamical system. We introduce a novel dual-LTC architecture comprising a Center-of-Mass (CoM) subsystem and a Base-of-Support (BoS) subsystem, both instantiated as Liquid Time-Constant (LTC) neural networks to continuously model inertial trajectory evolution and ground-contact adjustment through adaptive time constants, Physical interpretability of falling motion. A learnable coupling module emulates physical interaction between the two subsystems, while a Stability Manifold classifier operates in the joint latent space to detect boundary crossing via Lyapunov-inspired stability metrics. Complementary counterfactual trajectory projection and Time-to-Collision (TTC) estimation further enable irreversibility assessment and early warning. The architecture is designed to support a three-state prediction paradigm (Normal, Falling, Fallen); in this preliminary study, we validate the core stability discrimination capability on a two-class dataset (Normal vs. Falling), leaving the full three-state temporal transition to future work. Unlike conventional CNN--RNN pipelines, the proposed formulation encodes continuous-time mechanical inertia, yielding a sub-50K-parameter network capable of real-time inference on resource-constrained edge devices. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive accuracy with superior physical interpretability, validating its efficacy for low-compute visual fall detection.

Experimental High-Dimensional Quantum Overlapping Tomography

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (172 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2608.15795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large-scale quantum systems have advanced rapidly via the exploration of more particles and higher dimensions, offering great potential for developing quantum technologies. However, their characterization becomes prohibitive with increasing local dimensionality and particle number. Here we propose high-dimensional quantum overlapping tomography based on a graph-theoretic formulation, which allows one to efficiently reconstruct few-body marginals of multipartite high-dimensional quantum systems. We experimentally realize it on a photonic four-party entangled state in a $4 \times 4 \times 2 \times 2$ system. Using measurements in mutually unbiased bases, we reconstruct all six two-body marginals with only 25 projective measurement settings, compared with 94 and 225 settings for independent tomography of all two-body reduced states and full state tomography, respectively. The reconstructed marginals reveal a layered entanglement structure vital for high-dimensional quantum networks. We further show that these marginals enable more noise-resilient certification of multipartite high-dimensional entanglement than the fidelity-based criterion. Our work thus offers a scalable route for learning multidimensional quantum systems.

Latest Update: Statistical Adversaries: Natural Backdoor-like Adversarial Features in Clean Vision Datasets

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (161 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2607.05516v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Model-specific adversarial attacks have been extensively studied. We study a different failure mode: naturally occurring statistical signals in vision data that can behave as backdoor-like triggers without being maliciously inserted. We call these signals statistical adversaries. We analyse ImageNet to find patterns that are strongly linked to certain labels. We then use statistical controls to remove random correlations from our candidate signals. Finally, we demonstrate that these signals directly and predictably alter model predictions. These statistical adversaries are more targeted than generic corruptions and transfer across different model architectures. This suggests that some vulnerabilities are driven by dataset structure and distribution rather than a single model's idiosyncrasies. We conclude that ordinary datasets can contain exploitable adversarial surfaces even in the absence of poisoning, and suggest that dataset audits should treat spurious structure not only as a source of bias or interpretability failure, but also as a latent attack surface for vision models.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (184 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

de Broglie-Bohm Dynamics with Schr\"odinger Source Fields: A Framework for Subquantum Theory

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (184 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2608.13894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend de Broglie--Bohm (dBB) pilot-wave theory by introducing a complex source field into the Schr\"odinger equation and examining its effects on quantum equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics. In dBB theory, the physical particle distribution P, rather than the Born density $|{\psi}|^2$, carries the ensemble probability, so a source term may modify the pilot wave without violating conservation of total particle probability. We derive the source-modified Hamilton--Jacobi and continuity equations, the transport equation for the nonequilibrium ratio $f=P/|{\psi}|^2$, and an exact entropy-production formula. Three applications follow. First, suitably designed sources can drive exponential relaxation toward quantum equilibrium. Second, the entropy-production rate admits a Prigogine-type bilinear form, providing a basis for a subquantum thermodynamics with entropy-producing and entropy-extracting regimes. Third, a tuned source can exactly cancel the Bohmian quantum potential, yielding classical particle trajectories while the guiding wave retains nontrivial structure and the nonequilibrium ratio remains conserved. The resulting framework provides a unified setting for studying source-driven quantum nonequilibrium, entropy exchange, and classicalization, and motivates further investigation of the physical and ontological status of the source field.

Spatiotemporal and Multi-Robot Motion Planning on Graphs of Space-Time Convex Sets

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (220 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Industry observers note that arXiv:2607.00444v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decoupled multi-robot motion planning avoids the high-dimensional joint configuration space but requires repeated single-robot planning among moving obstacles, where route choice and timing are coupled. We develop a framework based on graphs of space-time convex sets (ST-GCSs) for continuous spatiotemporal planning and multi-robot coordination. An ST-GCS represents collision-free space-time by convex sets, allowing the sequence of regions and the geometry and timing of piecewise-linear trajectories to be optimized jointly under velocity limits. To incorporate moving obstacles and previously planned robots, we develop Exact Convex Decomposition (ECD), which removes their swept occupancies while maintaining a convex decomposition for subsequent planning queries. Building on path-based GCS search, we develop a best-first solver tailored to the ST-GCS motion model, exploiting temporal reachability for dominance pruning and using admissible heuristics with separate or joint search-key evaluation. Precomputed heuristic bounds can also be reused across reservation-updated graphs. We integrate ST-GCS planning and ECD into prioritized multi-robot planning and introduce windowed coordination with dynamic window adjustment to limit reservation-induced graph growth. Experiments demonstrate improved scalability and competitive solution quality against optimization-based and sampling-based planners on challenging spatiotemporal and multi-robot problems. Large-scale simulations coordinate up to $100$ robots within a minute, while real-robot demonstrations showcase the practical applicability of the framework. Project homepage: https://sites.google.com/view/stgcs.

Quantum Circuits for Quantum Spatial Search on $d$-Dimensional Hypercubic Lattices

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (243 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2607.19151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an explicit quantum-circuit construction for quantum spatial search based on discrete-time quantum walks on $d$-dimensional hypercubic lattices and systematically evaluate its circuit-resource scaling. Although the algorithmic performance of quantum spatial search has been extensively studied, a systematic evaluation of its circuit-resource scaling remains limited. We implement the flip-flop shift operator using coin-controlled modular increment and decrement operations for position updates and a single $X$ gate for direction reversal. We compare four implementations of the position update based on the quantum Fourier transform (QFT), ripple-carry addition, multi-controlled $X$ (MCX) gates, and automatically synthesized arithmetic. The results show that the QFT-based implementation reduces circuit width and depth, while the ripple-carry implementation reduces the CX-gate count at the cost of additional ancilla qubits. We also extend the construction to non-periodic boundary conditions by introducing self-loops at lattice boundaries. We confirm that numerical simulations of the circuits reproduce the theoretical search dynamics for $d=2,3,4$, and $5$ under periodic boundary conditions and for $d=2$ under non-periodic boundary conditions. For $N=L^d$ lattice sites, the circuit width scales as $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$. We derive asymptotic upper bounds on the total circuit depth of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{N}\log^{5/2} N)$ for $d=2$ and $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{N}\log^2 N)$ for $d\geq3$, consistent with the numerical results. Furthermore, CX-gate depolarizing noise simulations show that reducing the CX-gate count improves noise robustness. These results provide guidance for efficient quantum-circuit design for spatial search on hypercubic lattices.

Offline Preference-Based Trajectory Evaluation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (142 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2606.17541v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Offline evaluation of agentic systems often collapses trajectories into a binary terminal success value, discarding information about partial progress. This, in turn, results in widespread ties that create statistical inefficiency by reducing effective sample size and weakening the ability to distinguish systems. We propose preference-based trajectory evaluation, an evaluation measure that compares pairs of trajectories directly by using temporal preferences between time-to-return profiles. We find that, across diverse agentic and interactive benchmarks, success-based metrics result in tied comparisons on roughly 75% of instances, while trajectory-aware preferences reduce ties to roughly 35%, improving discriminative power, ranking stability, and data efficiency. Our results suggest that benchmark saturation, often portrayed as the result of poor data collection or problem difficulty, may also be explained by the design of the evaluation measure.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (197 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Relativistic bound-state solutions for a non-central Schi\"oberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular terms

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (197 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2607.16265v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Singular interactions can reshape quantum spectra by changing admissible wavefunction domains. In this study, we investigate this mechanism in the Klein--Gordon equation for a non-central Schi\"oberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular barriers. Equal scalar and vector couplings separate the radial and angular dynamics. We solve the angular equation exactly on each hemisphere with principal boundary conditions and treat the radial equation with the Greene--Aldrich approximation, obtaining Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions and an implicit relativistic quantization condition. With this boundary realization, the equatorial inverse-square singularity splits configuration space into reflection-related sectors with identical angular spectra. Reducing the barrier to zero while retaining the equatorial wall selects the odd-reflection spectral branch of the regular full-domain problem; a single hemisphere has no intrinsic parity. The nonrelativistic limit recovers the corresponding Schr\"odinger formulation. State-resolved nonrelativistic and relativistic benchmarks quantify the centrifugal error. In a dimensionless relativistic example, the relative error in the remaining binding exceeds unity near threshold although the absolute energy error decreases. For NaH and Na$_2$, low-lying central-radial vibrational energies agree reasonably with spectroscopic reference values, whereas the global radial shape limits near-dissociation accuracy and gives an incorrect NaH bound-state count.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Efficient logical operations in quantum LDPC codes using simple resource states

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (221 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2607.16166v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum LDPC codes provide a substantial reduction in qubit overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computation compared to surface code, thanks to their high encoding rate. However, operating simultaneously on multiple logical qubits encoded in the same block is more challenging and may slow down logical operations. Prior work addresses this problem by designing complex resource states to perform logical measurements in LDPC codes. Here, we propose an approach that only consumes cat states. Whereas previous work on cat-based measurements focuses on a single logical measurement, we design a protocol for the joint measurement of $\ell$ commuting logical operators. The key ingredient is the design of a scheduler code determining the measurement sequence and allowing for the decoding of all logical measurement outcomes. Numerical simulations with the LDPC codes Q70 and Q102 of the walking cat architecture show a reduction of nearly $3\times$ in the number of cat-based measurements required versus the Viterbi method for measuring $\ell=20$ commuting logical operators. Combining our logical measurement protocols with a new variant of the CliNR partial error correction scheme, we achieve a reduction of up to $73\times$ versus the Viterbi method for random Clifford circuits. Our approach also applies to non-Clifford gates, producing a reduction of up to $5\times$ versus the Viterbi method for Toffoli gates.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (187 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (187 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.18267v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks: 2D/3D fitting from images and point clouds, 3D novel view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, and geometry/appearance editing.

A Performance Model for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (156 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Industry observers note that arXiv:2607.15426v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workflows are expected to underpin practical quantum computing, yet the community lacks a shared framework for reasoning about integration requirements. We introduce a runtime model that decomposes workflow execution into quantum compute, classical compute, and communication costs at two levels of analysis. At the application level, where communication overhead only affects performance, we use a communication-to-computation ratio to quantify its impact on runtime. At the real-time level, when communication overhead determines feasibility, we examine how decoding and feedback latency affect logical operation times and resource requirements. The model evaluates execution with allocated resources, excluding scheduling and resource management. Applied to representative workflows, it shows that the compute-intensive applications, including those requiring HPC resources, are largely insensitive to communication overhead. However, the model identifies when hardware evolution, such as faster quantum processing and greater parallelism, can shift this balance toward communication bottlenecks.

#84031. FoundCause: A Foundation Model for Causal Discovery with Latent Confounders from Observational Data

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (194 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

FoundCause: A Foundation Model for Causal Discovery with Latent Confounders from Observational Data

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (194 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2606.17516v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Causal discovery from observational data requires recovering directed relations and latent confounding without interventions. We propose FoundCause, an {\em amortized causal discovery foundation model} trained only on synthetic structural causal models that maps datasets to causal graphs in a single forward pass. A permutation-equivariant transformer alternates attention over samples and variables to model cross-variable dependence and per-variable distributions. Pairwise dependence and asymmetry statistics guide its attention, edge decoder and confounder module. The decoder separates edge existence from direction, while triangular refinement incorporates evidence from chains and colliders. Learnable latent tokens predict which variable pairs share a hidden common cause, and a masked input representation handles missing data. To our knowledge, FoundCause is the first amortized causal discovery approach for i.i.d. observational data to predict latent confounding as a separate, explicit output. On 14 real-world and semi-synthetic datasets, FoundCause leads 11 classical and 7 amortized baselines in average AUROC, $F_1$, skeleton $F_1$, and normalized structural Hamming distance ($\mathrm{SHD}/d$): clearly in $\mathrm{SHD}/d$ ($0.875$ vs.\ $0.956$), narrowly in $F_1$ ($0.531$ vs.\ $0.516$). It also has the highest accuracy among amortized methods on bivariate cause--effect pairs.

Electrons Hopping across a Molecular Network: Spectra and Symmetries

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (141 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2607.14687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed for rings with $L=3,4,5,6$ nodes, filled with one, two or three electrons. Special attention is devoted to the role of the network symmetries in determining the structure of the many-body spectrum and the Mulliken classification of the eigenstates. Using group-theoretical methods, we examine the evolution of the spectra in the presence of an external magnetic flux. The Zeeman effect lifts degeneracies and results in combination with the Coulomb interaction to avoided crossings in symmetry sectors. We identify a qualitatively distinction between systems with an even and odd number of particles. At half-filling, particle-hole symmetry (duality) protects selected symmetry sectors against Zeeman splitting.

#84022. Insecurity of Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (187 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Insecurity of Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (187 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Industry observers note that arXiv:2607.01989v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The security of practical quantum key distribution (QKD) systems is fundamentally constrained by vulnerabilities of single-photon detectors. Measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) was proposed to remove this limitation by allowing all measurements to be performed by a completely untrusted party, under the assumption that the measurement node can be treated as adversarial but does not compromise the security guarantees of the protocol. Here we show that this assumption is insufficient under realistic adversarial control of the measurement device. We present an attack in which an adversary exploits active control of the measurement node (Charlie) to obtain significant information about the secret key. The attack enables recovery of up to 70\% of the sifted key while introducing only 5.6\% quantum bit error rate. Unlike previously reported attacks targeting specific implementations of MDI-QKD, our results demonstrate a limitation of the standard security model underlying the protocol. These findings indicate that additional constraints on the measurement-device independence assumption, or refined security analyses incorporating stronger adversarial capabilities, are required to ensure the security of MDI-QKD in realistic scenarios.

#84019. How additional labels affect multiparticle indistinguishability of identical particles

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (184 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

How additional labels affect multiparticle indistinguishability of identical particles

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (184 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2606.29312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For two identical particles, adding labels reduces the total overlap of their label states and decreases their exchange indistinguishability as measured by Hong--Ou--Mandel interference. For more than two particles, the opposite effect can occur: introducing additional labels can boost multiparticle indistinguishability. We present an explicit seven-particle example in which additional labels increase multiparticle indistinguishability by $7.38\%$, as quantified by the symmetric projection weight of the seven-particle label state, while decreasing the mean squared pairwise overlap by nearly half. We trace this effect to the cancellation of collective multiparticle phases. Phases associated with one set of label states cancel those associated with the other, thereby turning destructive contributions to the symmetric weight into constructive ones. We also give sufficient conditions that rule out this effect. For any number of identical particles, additional label states independent of the original label states cannot increase indistinguishability when the original symmetric weight is at least $1/2$. Independent additional label states also cannot increase the symmetric weight of any number of identical particles prepared independently in the same mixed label state.

#84016. Smooth Inliers, Erratic Outliers: Frequency-Aware Mamba for Two-View Correspondence Learning

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (242 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Smooth Inliers, Erratic Outliers: Frequency-Aware Mamba for Two-View Correspondence Learning

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (242 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2606.04493v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When shown matches between two photographs of the same cathedral, people can tell at a glance which ones are wrong: a window matched to its look-alike jumps against its neighbors, while correct matches shift together. Two-view correspondence learning, also called correspondence pruning, asks a network to make this judgment for thousands of candidate matches, most of which are wrong. Mamba, a fast sequence model, now drives strong pruners, but it reads the matches as a plain sequence, and whether its scan can capture such agreement is unclear. We propose SFMambaNet, which scans the matches cluster by cluster, so that correct matches vary slowly along the sequence while wrong ones stay erratic, and filters the scanned features with learnable frequency-domain gates between its forward and backward passes. On camera pose estimation, outlier removal and homography estimation, we find that SFMambaNet outperforms spatial-domain Mamba baselines with about two million parameters. Contrary to the usual expectation that such gains come from extra capacity, we find that a parameter-free low-pass filter beats point-wise layers as large as the gates. The learned gates turn low-pass on their own and make the scan far less sensitive to how the matches are shuffled. Together, these results show that frequency is a natural language for describing agreement between correspondences, with implications for other sequence models that must read unordered sets, such as point clouds and graphs.

Latent Q-Barrier Shielding for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (175 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2605.25267v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Safe in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) adapts online from interaction history without test-time parameter updates while controlling episode cost under a safety budget. Under out-of-distribution (OOD) deployment shifts, pretraining-only safe ICRL can give poor reward-safety tradeoffs because the remaining budget affects behavior only through frozen policy conditioning, not an explicit action-level check against predicted future cost. We propose a latent Q-Barrier shield that learns a context representation, latent dynamics, and an ensemble cost critic before deployment. Without parameter updates, the shield infers context from history and filters or softly reweights candidate actions using the remaining budget and predicted future cost. We prove a conditional one-step barrier-margin bound over realized candidate sets, with explicit Bellman and latent-prediction error terms. Across five safe ICRL benchmarks, the shield improves deployment-time reward-safety tradeoffs over a strong safe-ICRL baseline: after a short context window, it achieves higher return in four of five benchmarks while matching or lowering average episode cost in all five. Code is available at https://github.com/kmj1122/q-barrier.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (274 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Measuring and Attributing Evidence Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Models via Symmetric Counterfactual Controls

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (274 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

According to recent reports, arXiv:2611.13006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) asked closed clinical questions ("Is there a polyp?") can score well by relying on the question rather than the image, and current hallucination benchmarks cannot separate true visual discrimination from editing shortcuts or shifts in the answer threshold. We introduce a Counterfactual Evidence Framework that pairs each lesion erasure with a shape- and tool-matched control edit elsewhere in the image, adds same-site ring controls, restored and partial erasures, degraded views and natural negatives, tests on held-out inpainting tools, separates discrimination (the Evidence Sensitivity Gap, ESG, and AUROC) from the answer threshold, and checks the labels with blinded physician readers and hidden-state probes. Across 507 main-test cases (1,115 views), nine frontier VLMs claim 41.1% to 61.6% of erased lesions (ESG 0.269 to 0.470), whereas MedScope-4B, a Qwen3.5-4B agent trained on automatically built counterfactual trajectories, claims 9.6% (ESG 0.758; p <= 0.001 in all 27 primary comparisons). Physician readers support automated erasure in colonoscopy, where frontier models still claim 45% of erased lesions against 1% for MedScope-4B, but call a finding present on 54.7% of pooled erased reads across all sources, which bounds what unverified erasure can certify. Across 12 pre-registered training or system arms and 270 decision policies screened under a rule fixed in advance, every apparent utility gain comes from shifting the threshold rather than improving held-out discrimination, and probes point to perception as the remaining limit. We also report a 0/48 pneumothorax failure on an external cohort; retraining with pneumothorax patients in every stage finds 53% of pneumothoraxes on new patients without changing the main-test results.

arXiv:2609.26105v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Prediction of pathological complete response before neoadjuvant chemotherapy may facilitate more tailored therapeutic planning for breast cancer patients. This work proposes a deep-learning model for pretreatment data only, combining apparent diffusion coefficient maps, dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and clinical variables. The study uses the public ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 multicenter dataset. The architecture employs EfficientNet-B0 pretrained encoders for image feature extraction and late fusion with clinical information. Multiple clinical variables were evaluated, including age, race, histological type, HR/HER2 subtype, SBR grade, and maximum diameter. Only HR/HER2 subtype improved the average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and was retained in the final model. Using stratified five-fold cross-validation, standalone apparent diffusion coefficient maps achieved a mean AUC of 0.79, whereas dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging achieved 0.74. Adding HR/HER2 subtype improved performance to 0.83 and 0.81, respectively. The final configuration, using both imaging modalities and HR/HER2 subtype, achieved an AUC of 0.86. These results support pretreatment multimodal learning for response prediction, although external validation is required before clinical use.

arXiv:2606.22530v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Liouville pathways provide the conceptual foundation for interpreting multidimensional spectroscopies but, in open quantum systems, need not remain independent under the reduced dynamics. Environmental interactions can transport amplitude between pathway sectors during free evolution, producing measurable changes in the nonlinear response. We develop a differential framework for describing this transport under parametric deformation of the open-system dynamics. When the environment selects a pointer basis distinct from the observational basis, the resulting basis incompatibility mixes Liouville pathways and produces characteristic spectral distortions. Using a Duhamel expansion of the Liouvillian propagator, we derive local response derivatives that reconstruct this pathway redistribution. For a two-level model with a rotated dephasing basis, a second-order expansion about a single reference point retains the dominant spectral structure over a broad range of basis \Rconcept{misalignment, while the global error grows to approximately $37\%$ at maximal misalignment. These results show how local response information captures the spectroscopic consequences of Liouvillian deformation and establish pathway transport as a complementary organizing principle for multidimensional spectroscopy.

#83992. PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (217 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

PEARL: Unbiased Percentile Estimation via Contrastive Learning for Industrial-Scale Livestream Recommendation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (217 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2605.21752v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recommender systems trained on user interaction data are susceptible to behavioral intensity imbalance--a systematic distortion arising from heterogeneous engagement patterns across users. This imbalance skews feedback signals such that observed interactions no longer faithfully reflect true preferences, causing models to disproportionately amplify signals from highly active users while underrepresenting others, which ultimately degrades recommendation quality and robustness at scale. To address this concern, we propose a nonparametric contrastive percentile approximation framework, PEARL, that models relative preference signals instead of absolute engagement magnitudes. Building upon relative advantage debiasing, PEARL leverages real contrastive interaction samples to approximate percentile relationships directly, without relying on auxiliary distribution estimation models. We provide theoretical justification demonstrating that such pairwise comparisons yield unbiased estimates of percentile-based preference signals. For broader applicability, we introduce a prediction-based bootstrapping mechanism for percentile smoothing to handle sparse and discrete feedback, alongside a generalized value-weighted formulation and a co-training strategy to enhance both modeling flexibility and representation learning. Extensive offline experiments demonstrate that PEARL effectively mitigates behavioral bias and consistently improves recommendation performance across multiple ranking targets. Deployed in a production livestream platform with a combined user base of billions, online A/B testing confirms substantial real-world gains: +2.10% Watch Duration, +0.80% Consumption Amount, +1.49% Interaction Rate, and -6.91% Report Rate.

#83979. MARBLE: An Agentic Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning and Visual Abstraction

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (239 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

MARBLE: An Agentic Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning and Visual Abstraction

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (239 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2506.22992v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A central challenge for multimodal language models (MLLMs) in real-world tasks is to abstract visual observations into structured spatial states and reason over how those states change under actions over long horizons. Existing multimodal benchmarks often focus on static question answering, where answers can be directly extracted from images, or assume symbolic states are available and bypass the visual-to-spatial abstraction process. We present MARBLE, a diagnostic benchmark for spatially grounded multimodal reasoning and planning across three agent environments: CUBE, MAZE, and BLOX. MARBLE spans 2D and 3D spatial puzzles under geometric constraints, dynamic layouts, and spatial transformations, with difficulty systematically controlled along two axes: observation format and planning horizon. Extensive evaluations show that frontier MLLMs struggle on MARBLE, with the strongest model GPT-5.4 achieving only a 7.3% average success rate across the three environments in the hardest setting. Pairwise ablations on the open-weight models identify visual-to-spatial abstraction as the major bottleneck: when models must infer spatial states from images instead of receiving human-annotated states, success drops from 50.7% to 3.7% for Gemma-4-31B and from 87.9% to 6.5% for Kimi-K2.6. The results indicate that models often fail to construct precise spatial states from visual observations before planning, a task that is straightforward for humans. Overall, MARBLE reveals the gap in reliable visual-to-spatial abstraction for frontier MLLMs and provides a controlled testbed for measuring progress in spatially grounded multimodal reasoning and planning.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (164 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (164 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2605.20242v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Efficient discovery of precursor additives is essential for improving the performance of perovskite solar cells, yet the large chemical space makes conventional trial-and-error screening inefficient. Here we show that LEAP (LLM-driven Exploration via Active Learning for Perovskites), a closed-loop framework combining a domain-specialized language model with active learning, prioritizes perovskite precursor additives under low-data conditions. The model extracts mechanism-relevant knowledge from the literature and converts it into interpretable molecular descriptors for uncertainty-aware Bayesian optimization. On an evaluation drawn from unseen literature, the specialized model provides more mechanism-consistent answers than the tested general-purpose models. In an expert-guided proof-of-concept study, two later-round additives increase average device power conversion efficiencies to 20.13% and 20.87%, compared with 19.25% for the control, and the best device reaches 21.32%. Because only a limited number of candidates are tested prospectively, these results provide preliminary evidence that literature-grounded molecular representations, Bayesian optimization, and expert assessment can support additive discovery for perovskite solar cells.

#83975. Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (228 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (228 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Industry observers note that arXiv:2605.14434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative retrieval offers a promising alternative by unifying the fragmented multi-stage retrieval process into a single end-to-end model. However, its practical adoption in industrial e-commerce search remains challenging, given the massive and dynamic product catalogs, strict latency requirements, and the need to align retrieval with downstream ranking goals. In this work, we propose a retrieval framework tailored for real-world recall scenarios, positioning generative retrieval as a recall-stage supplement rather than an end-to-end replacement. Our method, CQ-SID (Category-and-Query constrained Semantic ID), employs category-aware and query-item contrastive learning along with Residual Quantized VAEs to encode items into hierarchical semantic cluster identifiers, significantly reducing beam search complexity. Additionally, we develop EG-GRPO (Expert-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization), a reinforcement learning approach that aligns generative recall with downstream ranking under sparse rewards by injecting ground-truth samples to stabilize training. Offline experiments on TmallAPP search logs show that CQ-SID achieves up to 26.76% and 11.11% relative gains in semantic and personalized click hitrate over RQ-VAE baselines, while halving beam search size. EG-GRPO further improves multi-objective performance. Online A/B tests confirm gains in GMV (+1.15%) and UCTCVR (+0.40%). The generative recall channel now contributes substantially in production, accounting for over 50.25% of exposures, 58.96% of clicks, and 72.63% of purchases, demonstrating a viable path for deploying generative retrieval in real-world e-commerce systems.

#83969. AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (255 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (255 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

According to recent reports, arXiv:2605.12925v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluation of software engineering (SWE) agents is dominated by a binary signal: whether the final patch passes the tests. This outcome-only view treats a principled solution and a chaotic trial-and-error process as equivalent. We show that this equivalence is empirically false. We evaluate 2,614 OpenHands trajectories from eight model backends on 60 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Of these, 47 have enough passing trajectories to construct task-level process references, yielding a 1,815-trajectory evaluation subset. Among passing trajectories in this subset, 10.7% exhibit behavior we call a Lucky Pass: regression cycles, blind retries, missing verification, or temporally disordered exploration, implementation, and verification. We introduce AgentLens, a framework for process-level assessment of SWE-agent trajectories, and release AgentLens-Bench, a dataset of 1,815 trajectories annotated with quality scores, waste signals, divergence points, and 47 task-level Prefix Tree Acceptor (PTA) references. AgentLens builds PTA references by merging multiple passing solutions for the same task, and uses a context-sensitive intent labeler to assign actions to Exploration, Implementation, Verification, or Orchestration based on trajectory history rather than tool identity alone. On AgentLens-Bench, the quality score separates passing trajectories into Lucky, Solid, and Ideal tiers and further decomposes Lucky Passes into five recurring mechanisms. Across the eight model backends, Lucky rates range from 0.5% to 23.2%, and some models move by as many as five rank positions when ranked by quality score instead of pass rate. We publicly release AgentLens-Bench and the AgentLens SDK at https://github.com/agentlens-framework/agentlens, with a project page at https://agentlens-framework.github.io/agentlens/.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (230 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Skypart : Weather-Robust Cross-View Geo-Localization via Prototype-Based Semantic Part Discovery

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (230 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2605.11654v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The low-altitude economy is growing rapidly, increasing demand for reliable drone navigation. Common tasks such as delivery, inspection, and search-and-rescue rely on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), which can be jammed, spoofed, or unavailable. Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL), which matches an oblique drone view to a geo-referenced satellite tile, offers an alternative for autonomous localization when GNSS fails. However, current CVGL methods have three limitations: (1) global descriptors compress patch grids into a single vector, without separating cross-view-shared layout from view-specific texture; (2) altitude-related scale variation remains in the learned embedding instead of being marginalized as a nuisance; and (3) multi-objective training uses hand-tuned loss weights despite incompatible gradient scales. We propose SKYPART, a lightweight, swappable head for patch-based vision transformers (ViTs) that explicitly groups patches into parts. It combines (i) learnable prototypes that compete for patch tokens through single-pass cosine assignment; (ii) altitude-conditioned linear modulation used only during training, yielding altitude-free retrieval embeddings at inference; (iii) graph-attention readout over active prototypes; and (iv) Kendall uncertainty-weighted multi-objective learning that learns loss-group weights end-to-end. With 26.95M parameters and 22.14 GFLOPs, SKYPART is the smallest top-performing method in our comparison and achieves state-of-the-art results on SUES-200, University-1652, and DenseUAV using single-pass retrieval without reranking or test-time augmentation (TTA). Its accuracy advantage over the strongest baseline further increases under ten WeatherPrompt corruption conditions. Code: https://github.com/chisngyen/SkyPart.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Radiative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient X-ray Novel View Synthesis

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (266 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2403.04116v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: X-ray is widely applied for transmission imaging due to its stronger penetration than natural light. When rendering novel view X-ray projections, existing methods mainly based on NeRF suffer from long training time and slow inference speed. In this paper, we propose a 3D Gaussian splatting-based method, namely X-Gaussian, for X-ray 3D reconstruction. Firstly, we redesign a radiative Gaussian point cloud model inspired by the isotropic nature of X-ray imaging. Our model excludes the influence of view direction when learning to predict the radiation intensity of 3D points. Based on this model, we develop a Differentiable Radiative Rasterization (DRR) with CUDA implementation. Secondly, we formulate a principled Radiative Gaussian Volume Querying (RGVQ) method that defines a continuous attenuation field from the original radiative point attributes and enables direct CT volume reconstruction through CUDA-based parallel querying. Thirdly, we customize an Angle-pose Cuboid Uniform Initialization (ACUI) strategy that directly uses the parameters of the X-ray scanner to compute the camera information and then uniformly samples point positions within a cuboid enclosing the scanned object. On novel view synthesis, X-Gaussian outperforms SOTA methods by 6.5 dB while enjoying less than 15% training time and over 73x inference speed. On CT reconstruction, X-Gaussian outperforms SOTA methods by 0.40 dB and 4.34 dB on synthetic and real scenes, while achieving 4.30x faster inference of the learned CT volume. Code, models, and datasets are at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/X-Gaussian . More video and interactive visualizations are presented on our project page at https://caiyuanhao1998.github.io/project/X-Gaussian . We also built an online Gradio demo page on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/X-Gaussian .

#83954. iMuon: Intrinsic Spectral Optimization on Riemannian Matrix Manifolds

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (231 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

iMuon: Intrinsic Spectral Optimization on Riemannian Matrix Manifolds

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (231 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2605.09238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Muon and related norm-constrained optimizers, now central to large-scale learning, compute updates via a linear maximization oracle (LMO) over a matrix-norm ball in Euclidean space. However, they do not generalize cleanly to manifold-valued parameters such as low-rank factorizations, orthogonality constraints, or symmetric positive-definite (SPD) matrices. Naively restricting the Muon LMO to the tangent space (i) breaks quotient symmetries and (ii) couples the tangent-space constraint with an ambient norm bound, which obstructs closed-form solutions. We resolve both problems with a key observation: every Riemannian metric canonically lifts a unitarily invariant Euclidean norm to an intrinsic norm on each tangent space. The resulting intrinsic LMO is symmetry preserving and, under a structural condition on the scaled tangent space, reduces to a standard Euclidean LMO. Building on this, we introduce intrinsic Muon (iMuon), a unified framework with closed-form updates on the fixed-rank, SPD, Stiefel, and Grassmann manifolds for various unitarily invariant norms, including the spectral, Frobenius, and nuclear norms. We establish deterministic and stochastic convergence rates of iMuon with constants that depend only on the manifold dimension. Notably, on the fixed-rank manifold, the constant depends only on the rank, which makes the rate independent of factor conditioning and removes the runtime factor rescaling required by prior work. Experiments on LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs, image classification, and subspace learning illustrate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

#83944. Structure-Aware Sparse-View X-ray 3D Reconstruction

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (193 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Structure-Aware Sparse-View X-ray 3D Reconstruction

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (193 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

According to recent reports, arXiv:2311.10959v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: X-ray, known for its ability to reveal internal structures of objects, is expected to provide richer information for 3D reconstruction than visible light. Yet, existing neural radiance fields (NeRF) algorithms overlook this important nature of X-ray, leading to their limitations in capturing structural contents of imaged objects. In this paper, we propose a framework, Structure-Aware X-ray Neural Radiodensity Fields (SAX-NeRF), for sparse-view X-ray 3D reconstruction. Firstly, we design a Line Segment-based Transformer (Lineformer) as the backbone of SAX-NeRF. Linefomer captures internal structures of objects in 3D space by modeling the dependencies within each line segment of an X-ray. Secondly, we present a Masked Local-Global (MLG) ray sampling strategy to extract contextual and geometric information in 2D projection. Plus, we collect a larger-scale dataset X3D covering wider X-ray applications. Experiments on X3D show that SAX-NeRF surpasses previous NeRF-based methods by 12.56 and 2.49 dB on novel view synthesis and CT reconstruction. Code, models, and data are released at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/SAX-NeRF . Our project page at https://caiyuanhao1998.github.io/project/SAX-NeRF/ shows more video and interactive results. An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/SAX-NeRF.

Microscopic exceptional points in the post-selected open Jaynes--Cummings model

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (160 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2606.14982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Phenomenological non-Hermitian Hamiltonians track selected signatures of complex reservoir dynamics, while post-selected no-jump effective Hamiltonians derived from microscopic open-system theory reveal the underlying system--reservoir physics. We derive the conditioned Jaynes--Cummings spectrum and propagator at finite temperature using Moore--Penrose normalized generators on the full Hilbert space. Within the Born--Markov approximation, full Bohr-frequency resolution excludes exceptional points; partial resolution permits coalescence when transition splittings compete with relaxation and the reservoir responses vary negligibly over the coupled transitions. For zero-temperature examples on shifted resonance, where the bare detuning compensates the reservoir-induced differential Lamb shift, unequal independent losses produce an excitation-dependent threshold, while equal shared losses with vanishing cross Lamb shifts and an orthogonal coupling phase produce a threshold independent of excitation number within the partial-resolution regime. Our shared-loss examples show oscillatory conditional transfer below the common threshold, monotonic transfer toward unit population at it, and a lower asymptotic population above it.

AI & Tech ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

CyBiasBench: Benchmarking Bias in LLM Agents for Cyber-Attack Scenarios

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (194 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2605.07830v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in offensive cybersecurity. In this paper, we reveal an interesting phenomenon: different agents exhibit distinct attack patterns. Specifically, agents exhibit distinct attack-selection biases, differing in both the families they explore and the concentration of their efforts. These patterns remain relatively stable across prompt variations. To systematically quantify this behavior, we introduce CyBiasBench, a comprehensive 630-session benchmark that evaluates five agents on three targets and four prompt conditions with ten attack families. We identify explicit bias across agents, with different dominant attack families and varying entropy levels in their attack-family allocation distributions. Such bias characterizes agent behavior within the evaluated environments and provides information beyond aggregate attack success rates. Furthermore, our experiments reveal a bias momentum effect, where agents resist explicit steering toward attack families that conflict with their bias. This forced distribution shift does not yield measurable improvements in attack performance. To ensure reproducibility and facilitate future research, we release an interactive result dashboard at https://trustworthyai.co.kr/CyBiasBench/ and a reproducibility artifact with aggregated session-level statistics and full evaluation scripts at https://github.com/Harry24k/CyBiasBench.

Degradation-Aware Unfolding Half-Shuffle Transformer for Spectral Compressive Imaging

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (183 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

In a recent development, arXiv:2205.10102v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In coded aperture snapshot spectral compressive imaging (CASSI) systems, hyperspectral image (HSI) reconstruction methods are employed to recover the spatial-spectral signal from a compressed measurement. Among these algorithms, deep unfolding methods demonstrate promising performance but suffer from two concerns. Firstly, they do not estimate the degradation patterns and ill-posedness degree from the highly related CASSI to guide the iterative learning. Secondly, they are mainly CNN-based, showing limitations in capturing long-range dependencies. In this paper, we propose a principled Degradation-Aware Unfolding Framework (DAUF) that estimates parameters from the compressed image and physical mask, and then uses these parameters to control each iteration. Moreover, we customize a novel Half-Shuffle Transformer (HST) that simultaneously captures local contents and non-local dependencies. By plugging HST into DAUF, we establish the first Transformer-based deep unfolding method, Degradation-Aware Unfolding Half-Shuffle Transformer (DAUHST), for HSI reconstruction. Experiments show that DAUHST significantly surpasses state-of-the-art methods while requiring cheaper computational and memory costs. Code and models will be released at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/MST . An online Gradio demo is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST.

HDNet: High-resolution Dual-domain Learning for Spectral Compressive Imaging

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (215 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

It has been revealed that arXiv:2203.02149v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid development of deep learning provides a better solution for the end-to-end reconstruction of hyperspectral image (HSI). However, existing learning-based methods have two major defects. Firstly, networks with self-attention usually sacrifice internal resolution to balance model performance against complexity, losing fine-grained high-resolution (HR) features. Secondly, even if the optimization focusing on spatial-spectral domain learning (SDL) converges to the ideal solution, there is still a significant visual difference between the reconstructed HSI and the truth. Therefore, we propose a high-resolution dual-domain learning network (HDNet) for HSI reconstruction. On the one hand, the proposed HR spatial-spectral attention module with its efficient feature fusion provides continuous and fine pixel-level features. On the other hand, frequency domain learning (FDL) is introduced for HSI reconstruction to narrow the frequency domain discrepancy. Dynamic FDL supervision forces the model to reconstruct fine-grained frequencies and compensate for excessive smoothing and distortion caused by pixel-level losses. The HR pixel-level attention and frequency-level refinement in our HDNet mutually promote HSI perceptual quality. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluation experiments show that our method achieves SOTA performance on simulated and real HSI datasets. Code and models will be released at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/MST . An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (214 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Computational regimes in matrix-product-state-based quantum trajectory simulations

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (214 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

In a recent development, arXiv:2606.13779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficient simulation of open quantum systems is central to modeling noisy quantum hardware and many-body dynamics. In trajectory-based tensor network methods, cost is often associated with trajectory-level quantities such as entanglement growth or bond dimension. However, the total cost of a fixed-accuracy simulation also depends on statistical sampling and on how many trajectories can run in parallel. Here we characterize computational regimes in matrix product state (MPS)-based quantum trajectory simulations by separating memory per trajectory, runtime per trajectory, and sampling effort. Two dimensionless ratios compare the bond dimensions and trajectory counts required by physically equivalent unravelings to reach the same target accuracy. When memory limits parallel execution, a smaller trajectory representation reduces the work per sample and allows more samples to run concurrently. Our scaling model predicts when this additional benefit reverses the preferred unraveling between execution limited by workers and execution limited by memory. Benchmarks across several noise channels illustrate how physical and numerical parameters change the bond dimension and sampling requirements. As an application, a pilot protocol estimates the inputs to this regime classification for a specified problem. These results show how the computational cost of an unraveling depends jointly on trajectory complexity, statistical convergence, and available hardware resources.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (203 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

Mask-guided Spectral-wise Transformer for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (203 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Sources indicate that arXiv:2111.07910v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) reconstruction aims to recover the 3D spatial-spectral signal from a 2D measurement in the coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI) system. The HSI representations are highly similar and correlated across the spectral dimension. Modeling the inter-spectra interactions is beneficial for HSI reconstruction. However, existing CNN-based methods show limitations in capturing spectral-wise similarity and long-range dependencies. Besides, the HSI information is modulated by a coded aperture (physical mask) in CASSI. Nonetheless, current algorithms have not fully explored the guidance effect of the mask for HSI restoration. In this paper, we propose a novel framework, Mask-guided Spectral-wise Transformer (MST), for HSI reconstruction. Specifically, we present a Spectral-wise Multi-head Self-Attention (S-MSA) that treats each spectral feature as a token and calculates self-attention along the spectral dimension. In addition, we customize a Mask-guided Mechanism (MM) that directs S-MSA to pay attention to spatial regions with high-fidelity spectral representations. Extensive experiments show that our MST significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods on simulation and real HSI datasets while requiring dramatically cheaper computational and memory costs. Code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/MST/ . An online Gradio demo is available on HuggingFace at https://huggingface.co/spaces/CaiYuanhao/MST.

#83912. When VLMs 'Fix' Students: Identifying and Penalizing Over-Correction in the Evaluation of Multi-line Handwritten Math OCR

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (205 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arxiv ↗ Open Full Page

When VLMs 'Fix' Students: Identifying and Penalizing Over-Correction in the Evaluation of Multi-line Handwritten Math OCR

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (205 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2604.22774v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate transcription of handwritten mathematics is crucial for educational AI systems, yet current benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability properly. Most prior studies focus on single-line expressions and rely on lexical metrics such as BLEU, which fail to assess the semantic reasoning across multi-line student solutions. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of multi-line handwritten math Optical Character Recognition (OCR), revealing a critical failure mode of Vision-Language Models (VLMs): over-correction. Instead of faithfully transcribing a student's work, these models often "fix" errors, thereby hiding the very mistakes an educational assessment aims to detect. To address this, we propose PINK (Penalized INK-based score), a semantic evaluation metric that leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for rubric-based grading and explicitly penalizes over-correction. Our comprehensive evaluation of 15 state-of-the-art VLMs on the FERMAT dataset reveals substantial ranking reversals compared to BLEU: models like GPT-4o are heavily penalized for aggressive over-correction, whereas Gemini 2.5 Flash emerges as the most faithful transcriber. Furthermore, human expert studies show that PINK aligns significantly better with human judgment (55.0% preference over BLEU's 39.5%), providing a more reliable evaluation framework for handwritten math OCR in educational settings. We further explore potential energy landscapes through 1D scans for H$_2$ and HeH$^+$ using both STO-3G and 6-31G basis sets, and for LiH and BeH$_2$ in STO-3G. Extending beyond this, we demonstrate the experimental construction of a full 2D potential energy surface for the water molecule on quantum hardware, mapped over a 32 $\times$ 32 grid in bond length and bond angle. To move beyond small benchmark systems, we combine SQD(LUCJ) with Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) to compute active-space energies for a set of ligand-like molecules, as well as the pharmacologically relevant amantadine system. Across all studies, the majority of quantum-computed energies agree with reference FCI results, as well as with DMET-CASCI energies for embedded systems, to within the chemical accuracy threshold for the chosen basis sets. These results demonstrate the reliability of sample-based diagonalization approaches and underscore the potential of hybrid embedding strategies for extending quantum simulations to increasingly complex molecular systems, while also highlighting their practicality on quantum hardware.

KINDRED's Model Context Protocol interface passed 22 distinct focused checks covering memory operations, authorization, and transport. Together, these results demonstrate persistent continuity with low recurring local-update costs through five million retained AMVs, providing working interfaces for applications and developers. The architecture keeps accepted memory available while reasoning is idle, allowing applications to invoke models only when tasks require interpretation, planning, or generation.

On these data, we compare post-training recipes that start from Qwen3.5-9B: training one model on the mixed data of all domains (MixSFT and MixRL), and training one teacher per domain with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), directly or after an SFT warm-up, and distilling the teachers into one student with MOPD. The comparison establishes MOPD of teachers trained with GSPO directly from Qwen3.5-9B as the best recipe: the student closely matches each teacher on its own domain and is on average above the mixed-training baselines on the same prompts. Since MOPD already merges the domain capabilities that MixRL would otherwise have to learn, its student is a stronger starting point for RL, and we ask whether the same data can carry the model further from there: we add MixRL on top of the MOPD student, on the same prompts and with the same settings, which, to our knowledge, no prior VLM recipe has studied. The same prompts still improve the MOPD student, with no collapse, and give our main model, M3OPD-Reasoner-9B. MOPD and MixRL can therefore work as consecutive stages that get more out of the same data. We release all data, the training code, and the checkpoints of every stage.

Industry observers note that arXiv:2603.12088v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Clifford Hierarchy has been a central topic in quantum computation due to its strong connections with fault-tolerant quantum computation, magic state distillation, and more. Nevertheless, only sections of the hierarchy are fully understood, such as diagonal gates and third level gates. The diagonal part of the hierarchy can be climbed by taking square roots and adding controls. Similarly, square roots of Pauli gates (first level) are Clifford gates (climb to the second level). Based on this theme, we study gates whose square roots climb to the next level. In this paper, we primarily focus on Hermitian gates, and in particular, we fully characterize Hermitian Clifford gates whose square roots climb to the third level.

Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

It has been revealed that arXiv:2512.02368v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Trajectory prediction is essential for safe planning and decision-making in autonomous driving. Map-free prediction improves deployment flexibility by removing the dependence on high-definition maps, but it also loses explicit road-topology and lane-connectivity priors. Consequently, the model must recover stable motion cues from short histories while resolving prospective interaction relations without lane-level guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a map-free trajectory prediction framework centered on a novel Goal-Conditioned Expert-Routed Transformer (GCERT). A lightweight intra-agent front-end first decomposes projected historical motion features into a smooth trend and a local detail residual through a centered moving average. Component-specific residual projections transform the two signals before a causal temporal Transformer summarizes their recombined evolution. GCERT employs dual-level expert routing: edge-level relation experts generate interaction-specific messages, while node-level state experts adapt the transformation after message aggregation. Predicted motion goals upgrade the node representations and construct prospective relative-geometry and orientation edge features before the final interaction layer, thereby conditioning attention, relation-specific message generation, and state transformation. GCERT therefore determines not only which neighboring agents should be attended to, but also what relation-specific information should be transmitted and how the aggregated node state should be transformed. The resulting representations are decoded into multimodal future trajectories and jointly optimized with trajectory-regression, mode-classification, and goal-prediction objectives.

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2603.10843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficient entanglement distillation is a central primitive for quantum information processing and future quantum networks. Conventional protocols rely on digital quantum circuits, requiring compiled multi-qubit gate sequences and fine-grained control that place heavy demands on near-term hardware. Crucially, leading network platforms, such as trapped ions and neutral atoms, naturally support coherent many-body interactions suited for continuous-time analog evolution. Motivated by this, we introduce the Hamiltonian entanglement distillation protocol, which uses information scrambling under native dynamics for analog quantum error detection. We establish a quantitative link between out-of-time-order correlators and distillation performance, showing that efficient scrambling directly yields high output fidelity. This capability is generic across interacting many-body Hamiltonians, with typical random Hamiltonians achieving near-optimal error detection in a constant evolution time independent of system size. Extending this framework to entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD), we show that analog error detection combined with classical post-processing saturates the fundamental 33.3% depolarizing noise-tolerance bound. Numerical simulations of device-native Rydberg-atom and trapped-ion Hamiltonians confirm that high-fidelity distillation is achievable within current experimental coherence times. Together, these results establish native analog dynamics as a practical, low-overhead route to entanglement distillation on near-term quantum platforms.

Visual Harness Scales General VLMs to Medical Images

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (210 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

arXiv:2611.22815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that an appropriate visual harness can substantially improve the performance of general vision-language models (VLMs) across diverse medical imaging tasks. We introduce VERA, a medical visual harness that equips general VLMs with interactive visual tools and systematic diagnostic evidence management. With VERA, general VLMs interactively explore medical images and progressively acquire diagnostic evidence, which is preserved in a lossless memory for subsequent retrieval and use. After submitting an initial answer, the VLM receives an assessment of potential omissions and the reliability of identified findings. This assessment guides further image inspection and measurement, followed by answer revision in an iterative agentic loop until sufficient evidence is obtained. Across 11 tasks and four imaging modalities, VERA improves performance on all tasks with Qwen3.8-27B, with notable gains in spleen measurement (63.3% to 98.3%), renal search (57.5% to 71.2%), and pulmonary nodule detection (0.0% to 28.2%). High-capability API-based VLMs achieve even higher performance with VERA. For example, GPT-6.1 Sol improves pulmonary nodule detection from 10.8% to 69.2% with VERA, demonstrating the complementary benefits of stronger model capabilities and an effective medical visual harness. Our results highlight the potential of visual harnesses as a fresh paradigm for scaling general VLMs to medical imaging tasks.
